verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce documents the delegated-credential core well. An agent creates a purchase-intent mandate (POST /acp/v1/instructions) that the user approves with a passkey, then retrieves an agent-specific token scoped to that instruction, merchant and amount; VisaNet enforces these at authorization, and the product claims it can confirm payment outcomes. However, Visa does not provide a checkout-session object, order confirmation rests on a single marketing line, the product is flagged as still in development and deployment, and no hands-on run shows a full purchase. Missing for 10: a documented checkout-session construct, a detailed order-confirmation or payment-outcome API, and independent hands-on evidence of a completed agent purchase.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can complete a purchase end-to-end — checkout session, delegated payment credential, confirmed order

citations.quote: During checkout, your agents display a list of the customer's tokenized cards.
A new pass-through payment token, specific to agents, that is intended for use at Visa-accepting merchant locations.
The agent requests the user to authenticate the Payment Instruction using their Passkey and provides that instruction to the Visa Intelligent Commerce platform.
Confirm payment outcomes and trigger post-purchase actions in real-time.
This product is in the process of development and deployment.
